title: The torsor class is the boundary of one
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [def-sc-zariski-site, def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Write $\mathbf Z_X$ for the constant integer sheaf. For every $G$-torsor $T$ [def-sc-gm-torsor] there is a short exact sequence $0\to G\to E\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf Z_X\to0$ of abelian sheaves whose *fibre over $1$*, the sheaf $E\times_{\mathbf Z_X,1}*$ of local lifts of the global section $1$ with $G$ acting by translation, is isomorphic to $T$. The Zariski bijection of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] sends $[T]$ to $\delta_E(1)\in H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},G)$, where $\delta_E:H^0(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathbf Z_X)\to H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},G)$ is the boundary map in the long exact sequence [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Conversely, for every such short exact sequence its fibre over $1$ is a $G$-torsor and its class is $\delta_E(1)$.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ (cohomology-lemma-torsors-h1), construction of the extension by pushout from the free abelian sheaf and its boundary of 1

proof.text: Starting with a G-torsor T, form E as the coproduct over $n\in\mathbf Z$ of the contracted powers $T^{\otimes n}$, with $T^{\otimes 0}=G$ and negative powers formed from the inverse torsor. Concatenation gives E an abelian-sheaf structure, the exponent map $p:E\to\mathbf Z_X$ is a surjection, and its kernel is G; hence $0\to G\to E\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ is exact. The fibre over 1 is T by construction.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ, construction of the extension by contracted powers of a torsor

proof.text: The long exact sequence of the short exact sequence of Step 1 [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] gives the connecting map $\delta_E:H^0(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathbf Z_X)\to H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},G)$. By [lem-sc-torsor-h1-zariski-boundary-class], applied to this sequence, the bijection of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] (Zariski case) sends the class of its fibre over $1$ to $\delta_E(1)$. That fibre is isomorphic to $T$ by Step 1, so $[T]\mapsto\delta_E(1)$.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ, boundary of 1 in the long exact cohomology sequence

proof.text: Conversely, let $0\to G\to E\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ be any short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. By [lem-sc-torsor-h1-zariski-boundary-class] its fibre over $1$ is a $G$-torsor and the bijection of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] (Zariski case) sends its class to $\delta_E(1)$, the boundary of $1$ in the long exact sequence [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. This is the converse clause.
